_: Kill-check for the version-bump prose carry-forward (`asc-4f2w`, `dogfood/0075`). The defect: a type's prose is stored per VERSION while every reader reads it off the LATEST one, so a bump that wrote nothing over those columns left the prose on the row it replaced -- not lost, not deleted, simply unreachable, and rendered exactly like a type that never had any. `note` did that when v1's `text` became v2's `body`, and `asc` rendered the project's own last-resort type as `note -- no record_when given`, the same string the deliberately-guidanceless `hand_empty` prints, which is why nothing caught it: the surface that should have carried five lines of guidance was an ABSENCE, and an absence reads as design. THE MECHANISM IS ONE RULE APPLIED TO FOUR COLUMNS, PER FIELD RATHER THAN PER BLOCK: `inheritProse` keeps what the write declared and fills from the version being superseded every field the write did not name -- `description`, `record_when`, each field of `guidance_json`, and each property of `prose_json`. Per field is what makes the fix complete rather than half of it. Carrying a column wholesale when the write declared NOTHING would still strand every field a PARTIAL write left out: a v2 declaring a new `purpose` and saying nothing else puts the other three lines out of reach, which is `dogfood/0075` one field at a time instead of four at once -- so G10 exists to kill exactly that shortcut. NULL is the declaration of silence, never a value, and that is the boundary worth stating rather than implying: under this rule a version bump cannot CLEAR a prose column, because NULL already means 'I did not say'. That is not a lost capability, it moves the drop to `updateTypeProse`, the writer that owns prose edits and whose `null` per field clears one; it is also why `register-document.ts`'s `droppedGuidance` warning -- which existed to make the old silent drop audible -- had nothing left to say and was removed with this change rather than left to fire falsely. The rule is deliberately the SAME one `updateTypeProse` already applies to an edit ('null clears, undefined keeps', its `mergeGuidance`), reused rather than restated, so a partial write and a prose edit cannot come to disagree about a field nobody mentioned. The mutants are chosen around the parts that can be got wrong independently: whether the guard runs at all (G1), the guidance column (G2), its DIRECTION, since inheriting over a declaration would silently discard what a document says (G3), the two scalar columns (G4, G5), the per-property column (G6, G7), and inside it the two things that make it per-key rather than wholesale -- the precedence of a declared entry over an inherited one (G8) and the drop of an entry keyed on a property the bump removed (G9), which `canonicalProseKeys` refuses at the door for a declared key and which nothing would catch for an inherited one. Every killer below was read off `assertionResults` from a real run of each mutant, never guessed. NOT MUTATED, and said rather than left as an implied gap: the SELECT that reads the superseded row's columns is not given its own mutant, because dropping a column from it leaves `latest.<column>` undefined and every registration in the file then throws -- a mutant that fails everything discriminates nothing, and the four inheritance mutants above already fail if the column is not read. What that costs is stated plainly: a mutant that reorders the SELECT's columns without renaming them is not detected, and is not a defect this rule can have.
